why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items. Item 1: no verifier PASS/FAIL condition requires exact stderr wording. Check 3 asks only that "stderr has an error", and usage-message checks are under "Advisory (not pass/fail)". No condition sets a branch rule, a mutation test or a file-touch limit. Check 4 allows a non-empty diff as long as lint's code and behaviour are unchanged. The builder's "Do not touch src/index.js" and its suggested message wording are build instructions, not pass conditions. Check 1's "A file named twice is reported twice" follows directly from "checks every file named in order". Item 2: checks 1–3 (the behaviour lines) each run B with real files, stdin or a missing file and record stdout, stderr and exit status. None passes by reading the code. Only check 4 (not a behaviour line) uses git diff.
